idle: In 1971 we did this with a file and a prayer.
good_ice: Ice like '79. Don't tell Earl I said so.
bad_ice: In 1971 the ice was worse. Not much worse.
cold: Cold as '72. That was a cold one.
leaving_happy: Good night. I'll write it down.
leaving_angry: Not a night for the book. Good night anyway.

senior_hockey: Twenty pairs of edges and a bell to polish.
Ring it if they win. Ring it if they don't. No, only if they win.
minor_hockey: That one said thank you. Notebook.
pro_practice: The Dukes' trainer uses Velcro. I've said nothing. I've said a little.

first.say: Well. In 1971, the first thing a new man did was say hello to the equipment manager. Hello.

options.text: Hello, Pete. Thank you for all you do.

first_thanks.say: A body who thanks the equipment manager goes in the good column. You're in the good column.

first_rush.say: Everybody was in a rush in 1971 too. They're mostly in my notebook now.

say: In 1971 the ice was bad, and they fixed it by 1979. That's eight years. I don't have eight years.

gameday.say: Game night. Bell's polished and twenty pairs of edges to check. In 1971 it was eighteen pairs.

gameday_help.say: Hold this skate. Not like that. Like a baby bird with a blade. There.

say: Ah. Sit. I was just in 1979.
There you are. I wrote you down today. Good things.

bell_done.say: The bell rings true now. I rang it in the empty lobby to check. Doreen played a chord back from upstairs.

options.text: Fifty years, and still in tune.

say: In 1971... no, go on. You first.
What can the equipment manager do for you?

options.text: What do you like watching here?
What do you make of Ray?
How does the rink measure up?
The final's tomorrow. Would you do my skates?
Who should I sign? You've got the notebook.

y79.say: I started in 1971. We won the Aldous Cup in 1979. In between, eight years of losing to Kessler. You need the eight to have the one.

photo.say: In the drawer by the sharpener. People call it old. It isn't old. It's been there a while, like me.

notebook.say: Pencil, never pen. Names, and what they did when nobody was watching. That's the only scouting that counts.

events.say: Kings games, of course. But minor hockey Saturdays tell you who a town is. Who ties the little skates. Who yells.

doreen.say: Fifty years. She still thinks the 15 card is bad luck. It is. We've never needed it.

ray.say: Ray's held the Kings together with squares and stubbornness. Don't let him start a toast after nine.

rink_79.say: Better than '79. Don't tell Earl. Don't tell Stan, either. He'd cry, and he hates that.

rink_rooms.say: Hooks that hold. A drain that drains. In 1971 we dreamed of this.

player.say: The night before a final. Same as 1971. Leave them on the bench. Don't watch me work.

do.note: Old Pete sharpened your skates the night before the final. 'Same as 1971.'

drawer.say: The photo, a roll of tape from 1979, and a list of every kid who ever said thank you. Coaches should read that list.

gm.say: Look for the fellow who picks up pucks after practice. Kenny Szabo, for one. Same as 1971.
